summary: Iteration 4 (Multi-Profils Pro) fully verified. Backend: 47/47 pytest tests pass (40 previous + 7 new in test_iteration4.py) covering: GET/POST/DELETE /api/me/orders/{slug}/variants, POST /activate/{vid}, Pro gating (402 for non-Pro on add), Pro path full CRUD (Perso+Pro variants, activate copies to order.profile, public /profile/{slug} reflects the active variant), 5-variant cap (6th returns 400), delete removes from list, ownership guard (wrong/other-owner slug → 403/404), auth guard (no bearer → 401), and clean subscription seed/unseed. critical_code_review_comments: server.py now at ~1030 lines — split into routers (variants belongs in a subscriptions/pro router or a new profile router).

activate_variant does not gate on Pro after activation reversal: currently POST /activate is Pro-gated (good), but DELETE /variants is NOT Pro-gated. A user could drop back to non-Pro mid-cycle and still delete leftover variants — likely intentional but worth confirming product-side.
The 40-char label truncation in add_variant silently trims. Consider Pydantic max_length validation on ProfileVariantIn.label so client sees a 422, not silent trim.
Max-5 check happens AFTER Pro gate but the constant is inline — extract MAX_VARIANTS = 5 to a config constant for reuse in the frontend hint.
Frontend MyProfile uses window.prompt for label — poor UX + not testable via Playwright. Consider a small modal with an Input.
listVariants is fetched inside the same useEffect as analytics/leads; on initial load with no activeSlug it fires 3 concurrent requests once activeSlug lands. Fine for now but could batch.
No ordering guarantee returned in variants list (Mongo array order preserved — OK, but consider explicit created_at per variant for future sort/rename UX).

success_rate.frontend: 100% (btn-variants-upgrade for non-Pro, btn-add-variant + pro-badge for Pro after Mongo seed)
